newsitem.title: LATVIA: IMF SEES 4 PCT GDP GROWTH,TAX COLLECTION WORRIES.
newsitem.headline: IMF SEES 4 PCT GDP GROWTH,TAX COLLECTION WORRIES.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund(IMF) sees Latvia's gross domestic product (GDP) growing by four percent in 1997 and is satisfied with low inflation but says improvements in tax collection are too slow, the Diena newspaper reported on Monday.

"I think that GDP will grow by four percent this year, slightly less than the government's long-term aim to achieve five percent growth a year," Dimitris Demekas, the IMF representative in Latvia and Estonia, was quoted as saying in an interview to the paper.
Changes in structural policy, including tax collection management improvement, have to be speeded up, Demekas said.
Meanwhile Latvia is showing one of the lowest inflation rates among the countries in transition and maintains positive fiscal and monetary policies, Demekas is quoted as saying.
Consumer prices in April rose year-on-year 8.8 percent against 18.5 percent a year ago.
The privatisation situation has improved during the last year and a half with the sell-off of the big state companies currently under way, Demekas said.
Latvia should not slow down the pace of development and has to decide without delay on the economic model it wants to develop in the future, he added.
"The country has to decide in the coming year's time.. what services it wants to develop and what functions it will pass on to the private sector," Demekas told the paper.
